ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, square $ABCD$ has a side length of 10, and contains 6 identical smaller squares within. The vertices $E$, $F$, $G$, and $H$ of a small square are located on sides $AD$, $AB$, $BC$, and $CD$ respectively. What is the length of $DH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As illustrated in the figure:\\
$\because$ The side length of square ABCD is 10,\\
$\therefore \angle A=\angle B=90^\circ$, $AB=10$,\\
Draw GP$\perp$AD at point G, with P being the foot of the perpendicular, thus $\angle 4=\angle 5=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral APGB is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore \angle 2+\angle 3=90^\circ$, $PG=AB=10$,\\
$\because$ Six squares of identical size are placed within the large square as shown in the figure,\\
$\therefore \angle 1+\angle 2=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle 3$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BGF \sim \triangle PGE$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BG}{PG}=\frac{FG}{EG}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BG}{10}=\frac{1}{5}$,\\
$\therefore GB=2$,\\
$\therefore AP=2$,\\
Similarly, $DE=2$,\\
$\therefore PE=AD-AP-DE=6$,\\
$\therefore EG=\sqrt{10^2+6^2}=2\sqrt{34}$,\\
$\therefore$ The side length of the small square is $\frac{2\sqrt{34}}{5}$,\\
$\therefore DH=\sqrt{EH^2-DE^2}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{2\sqrt{34}}{5}\right)^2-2^2}=\boxed{\frac{6}{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the outside is square ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, D is at the upper left, and the side length is 10. Inside there are 6 congruent small squares tilted and arranged into an oblique band from near the upper left to near the lower right. It can be seen that a vertex E of a small square is on side AD, and H is on side CD; there are also vertices F on side AB and G on side BC. In the figure, the oblique polyline/straight-line direction from E to G consists of 5 equal small-square side lengths, and EH and FG are exposed small-square sides in the same direction. Reasoning: Let DH=x, DE=y. Because EH is a small-square side, its horizontal projection is DH=x, and its vertical projection is DE=y. The other direction of small-square side perpendicular to EH, namely each segment advancing along the oblique band from E to G, has horizontal projection y and downward vertical projection x. In the figure, from the left side AD to the right side BC, it crosses 5 such segments in total, so the total horizontal projection is 5y. The distance between the left and right sides of the large square is 10, therefore 5y=10, giving y=2. Also because FG and EH are parallel and congruent, the corresponding endpoint relation near the bottom side BC for G makes the vertical distance of G above the bottom side also y=2; E is at distance y=2 below the top side. Therefore the total vertical drop from E to G is 10-2y=10-4=6. This vertical drop also equals the sum of the vertical projection x of each of the 5 segments, namely 5x=6, so x=6/5. Since x=DH, therefore DH=6/5.

From the image, read that the six congruent tilted squares form a strip in which the straight slanted run from E on AD to G on BC is made of five equal small-square side lengths, and that EH and FG are parallel exposed sides of the same small-square orientation. From the text, use that ABCD is a square of side 10 and that E,H,F,G lie on the four sides as shown. Let DH=x and DE=y. Then the side EH has horizontal/vertical projections (x,y). raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, square $ABCD$ has a side length of 10, and contains 6 identical smaller squares within. The vertices $E$, $F$, $G$, and $H$ of a small square are located on sides $AD$, $AB$, $BC$, and $CD$ respectively. What is the length of $DH$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As illustrated in the figure:\\
$\because$ The side length of square ABCD is 10,\\
$\therefore \angle A=\angle B=90^\circ$, $AB=10$,\\
Draw GP$\perp$AD at point G, with P being the foot of the perpendicular, thus $\angle 4=\angle 5=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral APGB is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore \angle 2+\angle 3=90^\circ$, $PG=AB=10$,\\
$\because$ Six squares of identical size are placed within the large square as shown in the figure,\\
$\therefore \angle 1+\angle 2=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle 3$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BGF \sim \triangle PGE$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BG}{PG}=\frac{FG}{EG}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BG}{10}=\frac{1}{5}$,\\
$\therefore GB=2$,\\
$\therefore AP=2$,\\
Similarly, $DE=2$,\\
$\therefore PE=AD-AP-DE=6$,\\
$\therefore EG=\sqrt{10^2+6^2}=2\sqrt{34}$,\\
$\therefore$ The side length of the small square is $\frac{2\sqrt{34}}{5}$,\\
$\therefore DH=\sqrt{EH^2-DE^2}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{2\sqrt{34}}{5}\right)^2-2^2}=\boxed{\frac{6}{5}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the outside is square ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, D is at the upper left, and the side length is 10. Inside there are 6 congruent small squares tilted and arranged into an oblique band from near the upper left to near the lower right. It can be seen that a vertex E of a small square is on side AD, and H is on side CD; there are also vertices F on side AB and G on side BC. In the figure, the oblique polyline/straight-line direction from E to G consists of 5 equal small-square side lengths, and EH and FG are exposed small-square sides in the same direction.

Reasoning: Let DH=x, DE=y. Because EH is a small-square side, its horizontal projection is DH=x, and its vertical projection is DE=y. The other direction of small-square side perpendicular to EH, namely each segment advancing along the oblique band from E to G, has horizontal projection y and downward vertical projection x. In the figure, from the left side AD to the right side BC, it crosses 5 such segments in total, so the total horizontal projection is 5y. The distance between the left and right sides of the large square is 10, therefore 5y=10, giving y=2. Also because FG and EH are parallel and congruent, the corresponding endpoint relation near the bottom side BC for G makes the vertical distance of G above the bottom side also y=2; E is at distance y=2 below the top side. Therefore the total vertical drop from E to G is 10-2y=10-4=6. This vertical drop also equals the sum of the vertical projection x of each of the 5 segments, namely 5x=6, so x=6/5. Since x=DH, therefore DH=6/5.
